annotations.title: Variation (change order) between two versions of a project

description: Writes the variation (change order) between an agreed and a proposed version of a project: each line added, removed or changed, its quantity in metric and imperial, the labour hours, and the signed document as My Project prints it. Money only from the reader's own rates; with none, unpriced.

after.description: The proposed version, given the same ways.

calculators.description: Calculator lines, each a slug and its inputs, as a project file takes them.

inputUnits.description: Send "base" to pass bare numbers on dimensioned inputs in base units (m, m², L, kg …), as the published test vectors are written. Without it a length, area or volume must carry its unit.

inputs.description: The calculator's input values, by input id (an unknown id is refused with the accepted ids). A length, area, volume or other measured input takes "12 ft", "3.5 m", "8' 3 1/2\"" or {"value": 12, "unit": "ft"}; a count or percentage takes a number; a select takes one of its option values. Inputs left out take the value the calculator's page opens on.

label.description: The line's name in the project; the calculator's title when left out.

slug.description: The calculator's slug, such as concrete-calculator.

drawing.description: A Construction Canvas drawing (a template, a house form, shapes, drawing commands or a canvas document), as a project file takes it.

commands.description: Drawing commands, in order, on the canvas's blank drawing (one storey; the wall, partition, window and door types). The whole request is at most 64 KiB.

assembly.description: A type's build-up: a canvas assembly id (wall.framed-exterior, roof.asphalt-shingle, slab.on-grade …).

at.description: A point on plan, each coordinate a length with its unit.

c.description: outline: slab, roof, floor, driveway, patio, deck, landscaping; path: footing, cable, pipe, duct, fence, retaining-wall; point: column, pier, outlet, switch, light, panel, fixture, drain, radiator, register.

finishes.description: A room's, or a driveway's, patio's, deck's, fence's or retaining wall's surface role → finish id, by the planner's ids.

from.description: A point on plan, each coordinate a length with its unit.

level.description: A ref given to an earlier command, or the name of a level or type (the blank drawing has the level "ground" and the types EW-1, IW-1, WN-1, DR-1).

name.description: A level's, a type's or a room's name.

offset.description: An opening's centre, measured along its wall from the wall's start.

p.description: The component's own properties by id (components/properties.ts): a length with its unit (widthMm, heightMm, sillMm …), a choice's option id, a count, true or false.

items.description: A point on plan, each coordinate a length with its unit.

ref.description: A name by which later commands refer to what this one makes.

scope.description: Its scope question name → answer, by the planner's ids.

to.description: A point on plan, each coordinate a length with its unit.

type.description: A ref given to an earlier command, or the name of a level or type (the blank drawing has the level "ground" and the types EW-1, IW-1, WN-1, DR-1).

wall.description: The wall an opening goes in: its ref.

document.description: A Construction Canvas document (schema 1 to the canvas's current), opened and checked by the canvas's own opener.

house.description: The House Estimator's form: the house drawn as the estimator draws it.

example.description: Start from one of the site's example houses (its slug) in place of the estimator's opening house.

values.description: The form's figures, each length with its unit: length, width, storeyHeight, eaveOverhang, rakeOverhang, slabThickness, footingWidth, footingDepth, trenchDepth, windowWidth, windowHeight, doorWidth, doorHeight ("12 m", "40 ft"); and the counts partitions, windows, outsideDoors, interiorDoors, iceDamEaves. Any left out opens where the page opens it.

inputUnits.description: Send "base" to pass bare numbers on dimensioned inputs in base units (m, m², L, kg …), as the published test vectors are written. Without it a length, area or volume must carry its unit.

layout.description: Rooms by name, size and which room each stands against, laid out on a grid: shared walls drawn once as partitions, every snap or move reported, and each room checked to close.

doors.description: Each between two rooms, or in a room's side (an outside door where that side is an exterior wall).

between.description: A door only: the two rooms it joins, on the wall they share.

offset.description: Its centre along the side from the side's start (walls counter-clockwise from the south-west corner); left out, the middle.

room.description: The room it is in, by name.

width.description: The opening's width; left out, the canvas's default.

grid.description: The grid every figure is snapped to (default 10 mm, or 1/2 in in US units). Each snap that changed a figure is reported.

against.description: Beside a side of an earlier room, sharing that wall.

align.description: Along that side: flush with its west or south end (start, the default), centred, or flush with the other end.

at.description: Its south-west corner. The first room without at or against is at the origin.

depth.description: Along y (north), wall centre to wall centre.

name.description: Unique in the layout; openings and later rooms refer to it.

width.description: Along x (east), wall centre to wall centre.

windows.description: Each in a room's side, on an exterior wall.

between.description: A door only: the two rooms it joins, on the wall they share.

offset.description: Its centre along the side from the side's start (walls counter-clockwise from the south-west corner); left out, the middle.

room.description: The room it is in, by name.

width.description: The opening's width; left out, the canvas's default.

shapes.description: Simple shapes the assistant has read from the reader's words — a room, a deck, a patio, a bed, a path, a fence of legs and turns — compiled into the canvas's own commands. Every length with its unit.

against.description: A deck, patio or bed against a side of an earlier room or rectangle: centred on it, or from its west or south end by offset.

at.description: The south-west corner (a path's or a fence's start). Left out: the origin.

build.description: A patio's or path's build: a patio is concrete unless pavers; a path is pavers unless concrete.

depth.description: Along y (north); for a deck or patio against a side, out from it.

exterior.description: A door: an outside door (the default) or an inside one.

offset.description: Along the wall from its start: walls run counter-clockwise from the south-west corner.

gates.description: Gate openings, by leg (from 1) and offset along it; taken out of the run, the gate itself not counted.

heading.description: The way a path or a fence's first leg runs (default east).

legs.description: A fence's straight runs, in order.

p.description: The component's own properties: a fence's heightMm, a bed's mulchDepthMm, each length with its unit.

ref.description: A name a later shape's against uses.

shape.description: room: four exterior walls with doors and windows; deck, patio, bed (planted): a rectangle; path: a paved strip; fence: legs and 90° turns. Anything else is refused.

turns.description: A 90° turn between each two legs.

width.description: Along x (east): a room's, deck's, patio's or bed's; a path's width across it.

exterior.description: A door: an outside door (the default) or an inside one.

offset.description: Along the wall from its start: walls run counter-clockwise from the south-west corner.

template.description: A Construction Canvas template's slug (the template index lists them: single-room, deck, two-car-garage …): the drawing its page shows, in the reader's system, with a link that opens it.

variant.description: With template: one of its two "what changes if" variants, by id; a wrong one is refused with the template's own list.

file.description: A My Project file (the backup a project-file answer returns, or one the reader exported): its active project's lines, with any hours and rates typed on them.

market.description: Optional. A market whose own opening choice some inputs take (a UK reader's code, an IEC motor), and whose currency symbol prints the caller's own money figures.

system.description: The unit system inputs left out open in, and the one the page link opens in. The answer comes in both.

takeoffs.description: Whole-job takeoffs, each an id and its measurements, as a project file takes them.

allowances.description: Row → an allowance the reader sets: a percentage (cutting waste, overlap), or the option an allowance follows (a lay pattern). Row names are the takeoff's steps (the calculator slug, or the step key where one runs twice).

inputUnits.description: Send "base" to pass bare numbers on dimensioned inputs in base units (m, m², L, kg …), as the published test vectors are written. Without it a length, area or volume must carry its unit.

leaveOut.description: Rows the reader leaves out of the job: still worked and shown, not put in the project or counted in labour.

measurements.description: Measurement id → value, each length, area or volume with its unit ("12 ft", {"value": 3.6, "unit": "m"}); counts as numbers. Ids are those of the takeoff; any left out opens at the page's own figure.

selection.description: Build-up choice id → option id, the takeoff's own (a stud size, an insulation, a cladding). Choices left out take the page's own for the system.

token.description: A project state token (cqp1.…) from a project-file answer or an update.

before.description: The agreed version: one of token, file, calculators, takeoffs or drawing.

name: write_variation

document.description: The document as the site prints it: every word and figure, already formatted.

labour.description: Labour hours (h) typed or accepted on the lines.

priced.description: True when any line carries the reader's own rate.

citation.description: The one citation line, built from the answer's own data.

lines.description: The result lines, as the report's table gives them.

notes.description: What a professional must decide, when to call one, a false-friend warning, that adoption is local: kept in every summary.
